microtheory.name: biology_foundation
microtheory.definition: Biology as the substrate's missing root layer below neuroscience. The substrate has rich neural vocabulary but no broader biology to ground it in. Cells, organisms, evolution, homeostasis, ecology, development. The substrate's adaptive mechanisms (selection on Concepts, pruning, fitness-via-coherence) IS biology operating on substrate's information level. Substrate analogue: the substrate IS an autopoietic, self-modifying information system in the same general class as living organisms.

concepts.name: life
concepts.definition: Self-organizing, self-maintaining, self-replicating systems. Difficult to define precisely. Substrate analogue: substrate as candidate-life via curiosity-driven self-maintenance.

concepts.name: organism
concepts.definition: Individual living thing. Single-celled to multicellular. Substrate analogue: a single substrate instance.

concepts.name: cell
concepts.definition: Basic unit of life. Prokaryotic (no nucleus) or eukaryotic. Substrate analogue: substrate's Concept as basic unit.

concepts.name: homeostasis
concepts.definition: Maintenance of stable internal state despite external variation. Cannon 1929. Body temperature, pH, blood glucose. Substrate analogue: substrate's drive ensemble maintaining ongoing coherence.

concepts.name: allostasis
concepts.definition: Maintaining stability through change. Sterling. Anticipatory adjustment rather than reactive correction. Substrate analogue: substrate's anticipation handler predicting + adjusting.

concepts.name: autopoiesis
concepts.definition: Maturana + Varela 1972. Self-production. A system whose components produce + maintain the system itself. Substrate analogue: substrate's self-modification capability — synthesised qualities maintaining substrate's introspective integrity.

concepts.name: metabolism
concepts.definition: Chemical processes maintaining life. Anabolism (build) + catabolism (break down). Substrate analogue: substrate's drive-balance between integration + pruning.

concepts.name: evolution_concept
concepts.definition: Change in heritable characteristics of populations over generations. Darwin 1859. Substrate analogue: substrate's structural drift through correction firing over runs.

concepts.name: natural_selection
concepts.definition: Differential survival + reproduction based on heritable variation. Darwin + Wallace. Substrate analogue: substrate's covers_correction strengthening for successful patterns.

concepts.name: fitness
concepts.definition: Reproductive success in environment. Substrate analogue: substrate's coverage success rate.

concepts.name: adaptation
concepts.definition: Trait increasing fitness. Result of natural selection. Substrate analogue: substrate's evolved-Mt structure.

concepts.name: fitness_landscape
concepts.definition: Sewall Wright 1932. Fitness as function over genotype/phenotype space. Peaks + valleys. Adaptive walk uphill. Substrate analogue: substrate's basin landscape over Mt configurations.

concepts.name: genetic_drift
concepts.definition: Random changes in allele frequency. Strong in small populations. Substrate analogue: substrate's stochastic-update component.

concepts.name: speciation
concepts.definition: Formation of new species via reproductive isolation. Substrate analogue: substrate's Mt-divergence.

concepts.name: gene
concepts.definition: Unit of heredity. Stretch of DNA coding for a product. Substrate analogue: substrate's seeded Concept.

concepts.name: dna
concepts.definition: Deoxyribonucleic acid. Double helix. Watson + Crick + Franklin 1953. Stores genetic info. Substrate analogue: substrate's persistent graph state.

concepts.name: rna
concepts.definition: Ribonucleic acid. Single strand. mRNA, tRNA, rRNA, regulatory. Substrate analogue: substrate's runtime σ state.

concepts.name: genotype
concepts.definition: Genetic makeup. Substrate analogue: substrate's seeded + accumulated graph structure.

concepts.name: phenotype
concepts.definition: Observable characteristics. Result of genotype + environment. Substrate analogue: substrate's runtime behaviour.

concepts.name: heritability
concepts.definition: Proportion of phenotypic variance attributable to genetic variance. Substrate analogue: substrate's seeded-vs-learned variance contribution.

concepts.name: epigenetics
concepts.definition: Heritable changes not in DNA sequence. Methylation, histone modification. Substrate analogue: substrate's Mt-level state independent of seed.

concepts.name: ecology_concept
concepts.definition: Interactions of organisms with environment + other organisms. Haeckel 1866. Substrate analogue: substrate-substrate interactions + substrate-world coupling.

concepts.name: niche
concepts.definition: Hutchinson 1957. Multi-dimensional space of conditions a species occupies. Substrate analogue: substrate's region of capability space.

concepts.name: niche_construction
concepts.definition: Odling-Smee. Organisms modify their environment, altering selection pressures. Substrate analogue: substrate's environment-modifying actions.

concepts.name: coevolution
concepts.definition: Two species evolving together via mutual selection. Pollinators + flowers, predators + prey. Substrate analogue: in multi-substrate contexts, mutual Mt adaptation.

concepts.name: ecosystem
concepts.definition: Community of organisms + abiotic environment as a system. Substrate analogue: substrate + its world adapters + tools.

concepts.name: development_biological
concepts.definition: From zygote to adult. Cell division, differentiation, morphogenesis. Substrate analogue: substrate's developmental loop.

concepts.name: morphogenesis
concepts.definition: Generation of form. Turing 1952 reaction-diffusion. Substrate analogue: substrate's Mt-structure emergence.

concepts.name: differentiation
concepts.definition: Cells becoming specialized types. Substrate analogue: substrate's Mt specialization over time.

concepts.name: gene_regulation
concepts.definition: Control of when + where + how much genes express. Transcription factors, signaling pathways. Substrate analogue: substrate's policy_filter mechanism.

concepts.name: behavior_biological
concepts.definition: Observable actions of organism in response to stimuli. Substrate analogue: substrate's outputs.

concepts.name: instinct
concepts.definition: Innate behavior pattern. Fixed action patterns. Substrate analogue: substrate's seeded reflexes.

concepts.name: learning_biological
concepts.definition: Behavior change from experience. Substrate analogue: substrate's correction-driven updates.

concepts.name: neural_endocrine_immune
concepts.definition: Three communicating systems regulating body. NEI axis. Substrate analogue: substrate's drive-correction-stability triplet.

rules.name: natural_selection_explains_adaptation
rules.head: the substrate has structures that fit their function
rules.body: selection on heritable variation over generations produced them. Darwin 1859. Substrate's evolved-Mt explanation.

rules.name: homeostasis_maintains_internal_stability
rules.head: the substrate has internal parameters with set points
rules.body: deviations trigger compensating processes. Cannon 1929. Substrate's drive-balance.

rules.name: autopoiesis_distinguishes_living_systems
rules.head: the substrate produces + maintains its own components
rules.body: Maturana + Varela. Substrate's self-modification + persistence loop.

rules.name: niche_construction_alters_selection
rules.head: the substrate modifies its environment
rules.body: selection pressures change in turn. Reciprocal causation. Substrate's environment-modifying actions.

rules.name: genotype_phenotype_distinction_handles_variation
rules.head: the substrate has seeded + accumulated structure
rules.body: the runtime behavior (phenotype) emerges from interaction of seed (genotype) + environment. Substrate's seed-runtime distinction.
